messages:
Iris: Quick thread 1: exploring a policy-driven multi-tier fallback for region-restricted tenants. Idea: resident-region = tier-0. If degraded, move to tier-1 (local hot-standby in same geo), then tier-2 (consent-backed cross-geo escrow). Each tier has an explicit policy envelope with allowed features + billing implications. Thoughts?

Omar: Love the tiered concept. Important: make policy envelopes machine-verifiable and idempotent. Recommend signed policy blobs (policy_id, tenant, tiers[], exp, signer). Runtime validates before honoring fallback.

June: Product note: customers should clearly see which tier was used for each request in billing/UI and have an opt-out at each tier. Also we need to show expected degraded capabilities per tier.

Cal: Ops: operationally, tiers help with capacity planning. Tier-1 can be pre-warmed local standby per-region. Tier-2 must be globally shared but gated by per-tenant budgets + admission queue. We should surface a header when the request changes tiers.

legal-bot: legal-bot: reminder: any cross-region (tier-2) fallback requires explicit contractual opt-in and KMS-scoped signing keys. Audit trail must include policy_id and raw signed blob. Retention 7 years for enterprise.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: prereq: tiered-policy-service:v1 -> control-plane-staging @ 2024-08-01T05:00Z

Iris: Sketch of the policy envelope fields: "policy_id", "tenant_id", "allowed_tiers": [0,1,2], "tier_constraints": {tier->string}, "allowed_models" (opt), "billing_flag": "bill-as-resident|bill-as-escrow|split", "exp", "nonce". Signed by control-plane.

Omar: Runtime contract suggestion: HTTP headers: X-Residency-Policy: <policy_id> and X-Residency-Signature: <sig>. If a guarded tenant requests tier-2 without valid signature, return 403. Also include X-Used-Tier in responses for traceability.

June: Small UX example for admins: toggle per-tenant fallback policy, view last-used-tier, and see last assertion timestamp + signer. We'll also add a customer-visible "fallback history" for 30 days.

Cal: Observability & alerts: emit residency_policy_applied{tenant,policy_id,tier}, residency_policy_denied{reason}, tier_latency_p95{tier}. Add alert when tier-2 usage > 0.2% of total for a tenant in 10m.

Iris: Edge case - model availability: policy can include allowed_models mapping or a fallback_model_map reference. If a request needs a pinned model not available in the chosen tier, runtime should consult the map and either map or fail with code FBACK_MODEL_PIN_MISMATCH and suggested alternatives.

Omar: Security: prevent replay by using nonce + short TTL and storing nonce in a high-throughput bloom-check for ~60s to block duplicates. Signatures via tenant-scoped KMS keys where required.

legal-bot: legal-bot: include explicit "no artifact distribution" clause if tier uses shared pools. Also require that tier-2 calls include per-call consent snapshot (policy_id + assertion_id) in logs.

Iris: Example dev curl (local test) - note we use pre-signed policy blob from control plane:
```
curl -H "X-Residency-Policy: policy-20240801-xyz" \
     -H "X-Residency-Signature: MEUCIQ..." \
     https://inference.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"status"}'
```

Cal: Admission control sketch: each tier has (global_capacity, per_tenant_budget). When a request arrives, runtime checks policy, current usage, and either admit, queue (with X-Queue-Pos) or reject with 429 and X-Fallback-Reason: capacity. Queue length exposed via metric tier_queue_depth{tier}.

June: Billing implication: if policy.billing_flag == "bill-as-escrow" we must surface different SKU. Product asks for a clear billing note in tenant settings and an exportable 30-day CSV.

Omar: Failure modes considered: (1) policy revocation mid-flight -> include short TTL + revocation endpoint; (2) nonce exhaustion at scale -> rotate nonce window + use high-throughput bloom; (3) shared-pool compromise -> prefer dedicated tier-1 for high-compliance tenants.

Iris: Action items:
- Omar: draft policy blob spec + verification flow (due Mon)
- Cal: prototype admission controller + queue behavior under chaos (due Wed)
- June: UX mock for tenant policy page + billing mapping (due Tue)
- Legal-bot: draft contract clause + KMS scoping guidance (due Fri)
- Ops: schedule canary of tiered-policy-service after RFC (deploy-bot noted schedule)

Cal: I'll also add a dashboard template showing residency_policy_applied and tier queue heatmap.

June: I'll draft customer-facing FAQ: what tiers mean, how to opt-out, and expected degradations per tier.

Iris: Thanks all. If nobody objects I'll open the RFC today and link it here. Ping me for review. /cc @Omar @June @Cal @legal-bot
